work.title: Piano Concerto No. 2 in C minor

version.note: The performing edition is not identified. This file is the complete transfer of the first original side, not a complete movement and not a reconstruction from joined sides. The HMV label calls the movement Allegro moderato; DAHR gives Moderato.

performers.note: The HMV label uses Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra; DAHR identifies the ensemble as the Philadelphia Orchestra.

date.note: DAHR identifies take 3 as the issued master. The Archive’s 1930 date describes the issued record, not this session.

place.note: The matrix’s Take Date and Place table names the Academy of Music. Camden in the issue’s MARC publisher imprint is not adopted as a recording venue.

label.value: His Master’s Voice / The Gramophone Co. Ltd.
label.note: UK 12-inch 78-rpm pressing, manufactured at Hayes, Middlesex, England according to the label.

catalogue.note: First side of the first movement; the label marks it No. 1 and 1st Record. Internet Archive dates the issue to 1930; DAHR’s generated MARC imprint gives [1929]. Publication was therefore documented well before 1963, without resolving the precise first issue date.

matrixTakeSides.value: Victor CVE-48963, take 3; Gramophone face number 42-600; concerto part 1
matrixTakeSides.note: DAHR connects the master take to DB-1333 and distinguishes 42-600 as a Gramophone face number. The Archive transcribes A48963 as another disc identifier; it is not treated as a separate performance or take.

credits.value: Phoebe Pugh, transfer and metadata; Akin Gaddis, disc cleaning; George Blood, L.P., digitisation
credits.note: Credits are the Archive’s user_transferred, user_metadataentered, user_cleaned and scanningcenter fields. The carrier belongs to the Leif Druedahl collection.

date.note: The item was made public on 19 April 2023; this is an upload date, not a documented transfer date.

processing.value: Digitised at 78 rpm; preferred 3.3-mil truncated-conical stylus transfer, equalised with turnover 500.0; 24-bit FLAC master and VBR MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: The Archive documents four stylus transfers and identifies the chosen stylus in the preferred FLAC comment. Technical notes report minor distortion and some wow/pitch warble. No additional restoration or speed correction has been applied for this edition; measured pitch-class or attack estimates must not be read as reliable tuning or ornament counts.

digital.format: VBR MP3 derivative of the George Blood 24-bit FLAC transfer; one original 78-rpm side, unjoined

composition.value: Public domain in ordinary life-plus-70 jurisdictions.
composition.note: Rachmaninoff died on 28 March 1943. This concerns the composition, not the separately assessed recording, transfer or an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Territorial EU public-domain basis: sound recording published before 1963.
recording.note: Rule 3. The HMV DB-1333 issue is dated 1930 by the Archive and [1929] in DAHR’s MARC imprint; 1930 is the conservative documented publication bound used in source.rights. Its former 50-year recording term expired before the 2013 extension, which applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013. US public-domain status is not established. This independent George Blood transfer has no licenceurl or non-commercial condition in the consulted item metadata and identifies its own original FLAC and physical carrier. F. Reeder’s separate RACHMANINOFFPianoConcertoNo.2InCMinor-NEWTRANSFER carries CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 and is expressly excluded, not an upstream source for this audio. This is a territorial recording-term assessment, not a worldwide licence or a claim that the modern transfer has been freely licensed.

rights.creditLine: Sergei Rachmaninoff, piano; Philadelphia Orchestra; Leopold Stokowski, conductor. Recorded 10 April 1929. HMV D.B. 1333, opening side only; Leif Druedahl collection, digitised by George Blood, L.P., via Internet Archive. Territorial EU public-domain recording basis; US status not established.
